dedupe_keys.name: nequick 2 ionospheric electron density model ictp

description: NeQuick 2 is a quick-run ionospheric electron density model designed for trans-ionospheric propagation applications such as satellite positioning and telecommunications. It describes electron density up to the F2 layer peak with a profile of five semi-Epstein layers whose thickness parameters are modelled; three anchor points (the E, F1 and F2 layer peaks) are set by the ionosonde parameters foE, foF1, foF2 and M(3000)F2, which can be modelled with ITU-R coefficients or derived from measurements. The model topside is a semi-Epstein layer with an empirically determined height-dependent thickness. Producer: the T/ICT4D Laboratory at ICTP, Trieste, with the Institute for Geophysics, Astrophysics and Meteorology of the University of Graz. Coverage: global. Access: the ICTP page describes the model; download and licence terms were not visible on the page read, so check with the provider. Cost: listed as free, unconfirmed. Caveats: it is a climatological model driven by solar activity and does not reproduce storm-time disturbances. Simulation uses: estimating ionospheric delay and total electron content in GNSS availability and accuracy studies, including scenarios with elevated solar activity. Related record: the Galileo-specific implementation NeQuick G (model-galileo-nequick-g).
